title: Localized Excitons and Exciton-Phonon Coupling in Antiferromagnetic AgCrP2S6
authors: Jessica McDivitt, Dimitar Pashov, Mark van Schilfgaarde, Justin C. Johnson, Jeffrey L. Blackburn, Anna A. Berseneva, Swagata Acharya
abstract: AgCrP2S6 combines a low-symmetry thiophosphate framework with an antiferromagnetic Cr sublattice and nonmagnetic Ag sites, providing a setting in which covalency and magnetic localization compete in the low-energy optical response. We combine single-crystal x-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, lattice-dynamical calculations, and self-consistent vertex corrected Feynman diagrammatic many-body approaches to determine the structural, electronic, and excitonic properties of bulk AgCrP2S6. The material remains monoclinic between 100 and 300 K, with additional Ag-site disorder resolved at low temperature, and the optimized structure is dynamically stable. The many-body calculations yield a reduced quasiparticle gap relative to Cr trihalides, but the lowest excitons remain predominantly local: the calculated low-energy (~1.4 eV) excitation cluster is best described as a weakly bright, strongly anisotropic Frenkel exciton with dominant onsite d-d character and substantial ligand-assisted d-p admixture. Symmetry analysis in the C2h setting identifies this state as predominantly Bu and constrains its leading exciton-phonon coupling channels to Ag diagonal renormalization and Bg-mediated bright-dark mixing. These results place AgCrP2S6 in a localized excitonic regime in which the stronger p-d hybridization, relative to the more ionic Cr trihalides, narrows the quasiparticle gap, while the antiferromagnetic exchange and Ag-site dilution disfavor the intersite coherence associated with strongly delocalized low-energy excitons.
summary: This work characterizes the electronic and excitonic properties of AgCrP2S6, a magnetic semiconductor. By combining structural measurements with advanced many-body calculations, the authors determine that the low-energy optical excitation is a localized Frenkel exciton. This highlights the delicate balance between covalent bonding and magnetic interactions in determining optical response in correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the competition between covalency, magnetic localization, and structural symmetry in determining the nature of the lowest optical exciton in the antiferromagnetic semiconductor AgCrP2S6.
main_result: The lowest exciton is found to be predominantly a localized Frenkel exciton, despite increased covalency, due to the combined effects of antiferromagnetism and Ag-site disorder.
method: The research combines single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, lattice-dynamical calculations, and advanced many-body theory (vertex corrected Feynman diagrammatic approaches).
model_or_system: The system is the layered thiophosphate semiconductor AgCrP2S6, which features an antiferromagnetic Cr sublattice and nonmagnetic Ag sites, allowing for the study of competing electronic interactions.
key_observables: Lowest exciton energy (~1.4 eV), exciton character (Frenkel vs. Wannier-Mott), exciton-phonon coupling channels, and quasiparticle gap.
important_parameters: Temperature range (100-300 K), exciton binding energy (~770 meV), and the relative strength of p-d hybridization versus intersite coherence.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the material remains dynamically stable in its monoclinic phase and that the low-energy optical response is dominated by $q=0$ excitations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, band structure along high-symmetry paths, and detailed analysis of the exciton character, real-space hole density, and phonon dispersion/Raman spectra.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure moving from structural characterization (XRD, lattice dynamics) to electronic structure (quasiparticle gap) and finally to the detailed excitonic and exciton-phonon coupling analysis using advanced many-body techniques.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of exciton localization and the explicit calculation of exciton-phonon coupling channels provide a rich model for understanding how lattice vibrations modulate electronic excitations in strongly correlated magnetic insulators.
